rows.verified: Maintenance operations must be capable of being carried out safely.
Safe maintenance can require stopping, isolating and locking off machinery, releasing stored energy and supporting parts that could fall.
Maintenance should be performed by competent people with sufficient information, instruction and training.
Work-equipment risk depends on machine design, condition, guarding, energy sources, task, operator competence, inspection and maintenance quality.
HSE PUWER evidence is equipment-, task-, operator-, maintenance-, inspection-, control- and time-specific and is not an exact parcel-level machinery-injury probability.
Hand-arm vibration is vibration transmitted from work processes into workers' hands and arms.
Regular and frequent exposure can cause permanent health effects, while occasional exposure is less likely to cause ill health.
Hand-arm vibration can cause hand-arm vibration syndrome and carpal tunnel syndrome.
Early symptoms can include tingling, numbness, reduced sensation, loss of grip strength and finger blanching.
Employers must assess vibration risk and reduce exposure that produces health risk.
The hand-arm vibration daily exposure action value is 2.5 m/s² A(8).
The hand-arm vibration daily exposure limit value is 5 m/s² A(8).
Employers must provide controls, information, training and health surveillance where required.
Hand-arm-vibration risk depends on acceleration, duration, tool condition, grip, posture, temperature, work pattern and individual susceptibility.
HSE vibration evidence is tool-, task-, worker-, exposure-, control-, health-surveillance- and time-specific and is not an exact parcel-level HAVS probability.
A pressure system contains or is likely to contain a relevant fluid above 0.5 bar.
The Pressure Systems Safety Regulations 2000 are the principal legislation covering user duties for pressure equipment.
Users must provide equipment that is safe, suitable for its purpose and correctly installed, modified and repaired.
Users must understand operating conditions, fluid characteristics and the equipment's safe operating limits.
Suitable protective devices such as safety valves or bursting discs must be correctly set and kept operational.
A whole-system maintenance programme should account for age, use and operating environment.
Qualifying systems require a written scheme of examination and examination by a competent person.
PSSR aims to prevent serious injury caused by stored pressure energy when a system or component fails.
Pressure-system risk depends on fluid, pressure, temperature, volume, materials, corrosion, protective devices, maintenance and operating practice.
HSE pressure-system evidence is system-, fluid-, equipment-, operating-, examination-, maintenance- and time-specific and is not an exact parcel-level rupture probability.
